newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cera Bank says Indosuez Belgium deal final in May.
newsitem.headline: Cera Bank says Indosuez Belgium deal final in May.

text.p: Belgian Cera Bank said on Thursday that the takeover of Banque Indosuez Belgique was right on track and would be finalised in May.
"Up to now the timing is still unchanged," Cera chief executive officer Willy Breesch told a news conference on 1996 earnings.
He said the audit and drafting of the final agreement had not yet been carried out and planning of synergies not completed.
But working groups have been set up to determine the distribution of tasks between Cera and Indosuez Belgique, which will maintain its autonomy and change its name.
"We hope that in April we can make final decisions so that the takeover can be completed in May," Breesch said.
He said the synergies would also imply Cera's brokerage unit Nedee.
A leading Cera official said the working groups were examining whether the dealing rooms of Nedee and Indosuez Belgique could be merged. They might also cooperate on bourse introductions, he said.
Other working groups were focusing on corporate finance and asset management, he said.
Breesch said there was not much sense in both Cera and Indosuez Belgique being primary dealers of Belgian state debt and that one of the two would give up its primary dealer status.
But he said Cera, Belgium's sixth-largest bank, had not decided yet which of the two would pull out.
Asked about which one he wanted to stay on as primary dealer, Breesch said: "The one which makes the biggest profit...I don't have any sentimental preference."
Cera said last December it would buy 80 percent of Banque Indosuez Belgique from French Banque Indosuez.
